objects.original: Actual PBPS recursion on H=E×E and Ω=ℕ→ℝ with P=infinitePi Exp(1), the same global actual Z, R(x,p)=(x,-p), literal normalized ν_y=tilted(-Vy)×stdGaussian, and real clock expectation T_Z.
objects.reconstructed:
Fix a finite-dimensional real inner-product space E, with its normed additive group structure and a Borel measurable structure. Its dimension may be zero. Fix V:E→R, nonnegative-real constants alpha,beta, and eta:R. The derivative expression is the genuine second Frechet derivative D(DV)(x), evaluated on v and then on v; gradient V is the real Hilbert gradient.

For y,b in E (b denotes xRef) and a phase point z=(x,v) in E×E, define c(y,b)=y−eta grad V(b) and
Phi(y,b,t,(x,v))=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+sqrt(eta) sin(t)v, −sin(t)/sqrt(eta)(x−c)+cos(t)v).
Define g_b(x)=grad V(x)−grad V(b). Define
S(b,(x,v))=(x,v−[2<v,g_b(x)>/||g_b(x)||²]g_b(x)),
r(b,(x,v))=sqrt(eta) max(0,<v,g_b(x)>),
Lambda(y,b,z,u)=integral from 0 to u of r(b,Phi(y,b,s,z)) ds.
For u,e in the nonnegative reals, tau(y,b,z,e) is the infimum in [0,infinity] of those u with Lambda(y,b,z,u)−e≥0; it is infinity if that set is empty. The flow's time argument is real; Lambda and tau use nonnegative times.

Rec=([0,infinity)×(E×E)) disjoint-union {stopped}. A live record stores an absolute accumulated time and a phase state. Given a threshold e, next(y,b,e,stopped)=stopped. From live(a,z), next is stopped if tau(y,b,z,e)=infinity; otherwise it is live(a+tau,S(b,Phi(y,b,tau,z))). record(y,b,z0,eSeq,0)=live(0,z0), and record(k+1)=next(y,b,eSeq(k),record(k)). Thus n counts n applications of next; the state at a finite event is the post-S state.

P is the countable product on R^N of unit-rate exponential probability measures. For any sequence w:N→R, epsilon(w)(k)=max(w(k),0), interpreted in the nonnegative reals. history(y,b,z0,n,w)(j)=record(y,b,z0,epsilon(w),j), for j=0,...,n. Hist(n) is the full function space {0,...,n}→Rec. readTime(live(a,z))=a as a real, and readTime(stopped)=0.

Delta(n,T) consists of vectors (t1,...,tn) satisfying 0<t1<...<tn<T. In the literal zero-based notation, t_i for i in Fin n corresponds to t_(i+1) in this one-based display. Prefix(n,T) is the subtype of such vectors, and m(n,T) is Lebesgue measure on R^(Fin n) pulled back to that subtype by inclusion. Set t0=0. For t in Prefix(n,T), define z_0=z0 and z_i=S(b,Phi(y,b,t_i−t_(i−1),z_(i−1))) for i=1,...,n. This is zAt. Define K(t)(i)=live(t_i,z_i), i=0,...,n; the displayed Lean definition converts each time through positive part. Define qReal(t)=product over i=1,...,n of [r(b,Phi(y,b,t_i−t_(i−1),z_(i−1))) exp(−Lambda(y,b,z_(i−1),t_i−t_(i−1)))]. The exact expression passes each interval to Lambda through Real.toNNReal. Define q(t)=ENNReal.ofReal(qReal(t)). There is no terminal survival factor in q itself.

A(n,T) is the subset of Hist(n) in which every record is live, the entire sequence of readTime values is strictly increasing, and all times at indices 1,...,n are strictly less than T. For arbitrary members of A, the first time is not separately required to equal zero. Define eventTime(j) as the stored time of record(j), viewed in [0,infinity], or infinity if it is stopped. I(y,b,z0,T,n) is the set of w with eventTime(n)≤T<eventTime(n+1). Define N(y,b,z0,T,w) as the least n satisfying this condition, if one exists, and zero otherwise.

liveTime(live(a,z))=a and liveTime(stopped)=0. Set d(n,T,h)=T−liveTime(h(n)), with nonnegative subtraction (hence truncation at zero). survival(y,b,live(a,z),u,e) means u<tau(y,b,z,max(e,0)); it is false for stopped. weight(y,b,live(a,z),u)=ENNReal.ofReal(exp(−Lambda(y,b,z,u))); it is zero for stopped. C(y,b,z0,n,T) consists of w whose history belongs to A(n,T) and whose next threshold w(n) satisfies survival for record(n) for the remaining duration d(n,T,history).

Path(T) is the type of all functions [0,T]→E×E, where [0,T] is a subtype of the nonnegative reals. For an arbitrary h in Hist(n), Psi(y,b,z0,n,T,h)(s) starts at z0 and visits indices 0,...,n in ascending order. A stopped record does nothing. A live(a,z) record with a≤s overwrites the current result by Phi(y,b,s−a,z); a later eligible index overwrites an earlier one. Subtraction here is nonnegative subtraction. Gamma(t)=Psi(K(t)). rho(t)=q(t) times weight at K(t)(n) for duration d(n,T,K(t)). These are literal definitions, rather than an asserted path-density theorem.

R(x,v)=(x,−v). Vy(y,x)=V(x)+||x−y||²/(2 eta). Let J(y)=integral_E exp(−Vy(y,x)) dx. The first marginal of nu(y) is the measure with Lebesgue density ENNReal.ofReal(exp(−Vy(y,x))/J(y)), using the exact normalized tilted-measure convention supplied in the packet. nu(y) is this measure times the centered identity-covariance Gaussian on E in the velocity coordinate. No extra normalizing symbol is quantified as data.

domains.original: All y,r∈E, all finite T∈ℝ≥0, all rank(E)≥0. F,G:H→ℝ are Borel measurable and bounded everywhere by finite nonnegative real C_F,C_G. No continuity, sign, compact-support, positive-rate or positive-horizon restriction.
domains.reconstructed: E is a real finite-dimensional inner-product Borel space, with canonical volume. Phase states are ordered pairs (position,velocity) in E×E. V is real-valued. alpha,beta belong to R≥0; eta belongs to R. y and b range independently over all E, and initial states z0 range over all E×E. The deterministic flow accepts all real times. Thresholds, stored event times, horizons, and process evaluation times are nonnegative reals; event times may additionally be infinity through WithTop R≥0. Indices n,k are natural numbers including zero. Noise samples are all real sequences, with the coordinate-product measurable structure and probability measure P. Histories have n+1 entries; prefix vectors have n entries. q,weight,rho are extended nonnegative-real-valued; rate,Lambda,qReal are real-valued. F,G are real-valued phase-space functions; their bounds C_F,C_G are real numbers. Z returns a phase point, not a measure or a path-space element.
domains.evidence: Finite inner-product Borel E including rank0; all y,r, finite NNReal T; pointwise bounded Borel real F,G. Canonical coordinate-free generalization is explicit; no restricted observables.

quantifiers.original: Original ambient parameters and six analytic binders; literal37 definitions; ∃one global Z with exact105 prefix; ∀y r T, endpoint measure preservation and ∀F G, Measurable F→Measurable G→∀C_F C_G, 0≤C_F→0≤C_G→(∀z,|Fz|≤C_F)→(∀z,|Gz|≤C_G)→the two integrability conclusions and duality.
quantifiers.reconstructed:
For every choice of E and its listed structures, and every V,alpha,beta,eta satisfying the outer analytic hypotheses, there exists a single function Z:E→E→(E×E)→R≥0→(N→R)→(E×E) satisfying all five clauses simultaneously. This existential precedes every y,b,z0,w,time,n and observable quantifier; it supplies one jointly measurable choice for all such inputs, at the fixed outer V,alpha,beta,eta and structures.
Clause 1 is joint measurability in all five inputs. Clause 2 is for every y,b,z0,w,s,n,a and is conditional on membership w∈I(y,b,z0,s,n) and record(n)=live(a). Clause 3 is for every y,b,z0,w,s and is conditional on nonexistence of any such n. Clause 4 reads for every y,b,z0, for P-almost every w, Z(y,b,z0,0,w)=z0; the exceptional null set may depend on y,b,z0. It does not give a common null set for all those inputs. Clause 5 is for every y,b and every nonnegative horizon T: both endpoint measure preservation and the following observable clause hold. That observable clause universally quantifies F,G,C_F,C_G, then assumes their measurability and bounds, then concludes two integrabilities and one equality. No almost-everywhere qualifier replaces the pointwise statements in clauses 2 or 3.
quantifiers.evidence: One global existential Z precedes all parameters, times and observables. Zero initialization remains parameterwise a.e.; test bounds are independent universal variables.

assumptions.original: Exactly the six analytic source binders. Observable measurability and boundedness describe the source test class. Probability, joint measurability, section integrability, Fubini eligibility and Gaussian flip symmetry are internal producer consequences, never new assumptions.
assumptions.reconstructed:
The ambient typeclass hypotheses are NormedAddCommGroup E, InnerProductSpace R E, FiniteDimensional R E, MeasurableSpace E, and BorelSpace E. The analytic hypotheses are: (1) alpha>0 after coercion to R; (2) alpha≤beta in the nonnegative reals; (3) V is ContDiff R 2, meaning twice continuously Frechet differentiable; (4) for every x,v in E, alpha||v||²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤beta||v||²; (5) eta>0; (6) beta eta≤1. These are global bounds, for all points and directions. They imply beta>0, but beta>0 is not a separately written premise.
The observable clause is conditional on Measurable F, Measurable G, 0≤C_F, 0≤C_G, and pointwise global bounds |F(z)|≤C_F and |G(z)|≤C_G for every z. The bounds are not merely almost-everywhere bounds. These observable assumptions occur only inside that universally quantified clause; they do not constrain the preceding endpoint-preservation conclusion. No further measurability, integrability, nonexplosion, positivity of holding times, normalization, or samplewise initialization premise is written. Every let binding above is a definition, not an additional hypothesis.
assumptions.evidence: Six original analytic binders and nested source test-class hypotheses only. No probability, integrability, kernel, normalizer or arbitrary provider premise.

conclusion.original: For the actual witness, MeasurePreserving e_Z ((ν_y).prod P) ν_y. For every bounded measurable F,G, both z↦Fz*T_ZGz and z↦G(Rz)*T_Z(F∘R)z are ν_y-integrable, and their real integrals are equal.
conclusion.reconstructed:
There exists Z as quantified above such that:
(1) The map ((y,b),z0,s,w)↦Z(y,b,z0,s,w), in the precise nested-product order of the packet, is measurable jointly in y,b,z0,s,w.
(2) Whenever eventTime(n)≤s<eventTime(n+1) and record(n)=live(a,z), one has Z(y,b,z0,s,w)=Phi(y,b,s−a,z), with subtraction performed in nonnegative reals. The rule is asserted for every sample sequence, not only almost surely.
(3) If no n satisfies eventTime(n)≤s<eventTime(n+1), then Z(y,b,z0,s,w)=z0, again for every sample sequence.
(4) For each fixed y,b,z0, Z(y,b,z0,0,w)=z0 for P-almost every w.
(5) For each fixed y,b,T, set Q_T G(z)=integral G(Z(y,b,z,T,w)) dP(w) and endpoint(z,w)=Z(y,b,z,T,w). endpoint is measure preserving from nu(y)×P to nu(y): it is measurable and its pushforward measure equals nu(y). In addition, for every measurable real F,G with the displayed nonnegative finite global bounds, both z↦F(z) Q_T G(z) and z↦G(Rz) Q_T(F∘R)(z) are integrable with respect to nu(y), and
integral F(z) Q_T G(z) dnu(y)(z) = integral G(Rz) Q_T(F∘R)(z) dnu(y)(z).
The same b is fixed in both operators. nu(y) depends on y,V,eta and the ambient structures, but not on b. The equality is a reversal identity involving velocity negation on both observables on the right. It does not literally state ordinary detailed balance without R.

scopes.reconstructed:
The result ranges over every permitted dimension including zero and arbitrary fixed initial states, reference points, centers, and nonnegative evaluation horizons. It specifies a total process by a bracketing rule and a fallback. It does not explicitly assert that a bracket exists almost surely at all positive times, that event accumulation cannot occur, that event counts have finite moments, or that stopped records have zero probability. The total definition and endpoint invariance are the literal claims even where such additional properties might be derivable. It also does not explicitly assert a semigroup property, a Markov property, path measurability as a path-valued map, right continuity, uniqueness of Z, convergence to nu, error bounds, or a path-space density formula. Auxiliary formulas do not constitute these assertions.
When g_b(x)=0, real division by zero is defined as zero, so S fixes the state and rate is zero at that state. eta>0 keeps the sqrt(eta) denominator positive. If e=0, the hitting set contains time zero because Lambda(...,0)=0, so tau=0, including cases of identically zero rate. For positive e and a never-reaching cumulative value, tau=infinity and next stops. untopD 0 is only used in the finite branch of next; it is not a replacement of infinite holding times by zero within that branch. Negative real noise coordinates are sent to zero thresholds. Such arbitrary samples remain covered by the pointwise clauses, while P itself is the exponential product law.
An event exactly at s is on the left side of the bracket eventTime(n)≤s, while the next event must be strictly later. At repeated event times, a bracket is not guaranteed at each index. If there is no bracket at a finite horizon, including possible accumulation scenarios, the fallback is z0. Initialization is only explicitly almost sure; it is not asserted for all arbitrary real sequences.
For n=0, Prefix(0,T) has the unique empty vector even when T=0; its strict-increase condition on the prepended singleton is vacuous, and the upper-bound condition has no indices. qReal=1 and q=1, K has the single initial live record, and rho is its terminal survival weight. For n>0 and T=0, Prefix(n,0) is empty. A(0,T) merely requires a live singleton record; it does not force its time to zero or less than T. N=0 cannot distinguish a genuine index-zero bracket from the fallback of no bracket. d truncates to zero for arbitrary histories whose final live time exceeds T. Psi on arbitrary histories selects the last eligible index in enumeration order, not necessarily the record with the greatest time; they coincide for the constructed ordered histories.
The supplied tilted-measure convention uses the real integral J(y) and total real division. It does not insert a premise 0<J(y)<infinity or a separately displayed IsProbabilityMeasure(nu(y)) conclusion. No such clause is silently added here. The packet labels the Lean statement compiled, but this decoder has not independently checked compilation, mathematical truth, or source equivalence, and gives no verdict on those matters. There is no source text or informal proof in the mathematical input. The interpretation of library primitives is limited to their names, the literal proposition, and the approved definition context; no source inspection was performed.

The deterministic definitions c,Phi,S,rate,Lambda,tau,next,record and the desired Z are parameterized by the fixed potential and step size. V and eta occur in their formulas; alpha and beta provide outer hypotheses. The existential choice of Z is permitted logically to depend on all fixed outer data and hypothesis proofs, since the proposition does not assert uniqueness or independence from them. c and Phi depend on y,b; S and rate depend on b and the phase state; Lambda and tau use y,b and the starting state. All recursions use the same y,b throughout. The noise law P is the fixed independent unit-exponential product, independent of those parameters; epsilon converts each coordinate to a nonnegative threshold. Each record n uses threshold coordinates 0,...,n−1. The bracketing event I(n) additionally uses record(n+1), and thus can depend on coordinate n. survival at record(n) also uses threshold n. nu(y) depends on V,eta,y,volume and the Gaussian structure, without b. The constants C_F,C_G may be chosen separately for the two observables and introduce no numerical constant in the conclusion.
Only the record construction, eventTime/I, Phi, P, R, and nu feed explicitly into the displayed final assertions. history,Hist,readTime,Delta,Prefix,m,zAt,K,qReal,q,A,N,liveTime,d,survival,weight,C,Path,Psi,Gamma,rho are auxiliary let-defined objects; their presence alone supplies no additional equality, density representation, distributional statement, or path regularity conclusion. Dependencies here describe syntax and supplied definitions, not an independently verified proof dependency graph.
